director.chapterArc: Escalating dread through three distinct environmental anomalies (Sag, shadows, iron) followed by tactical training and a shared grief moment before the chapter closes on an ominous discovery of gouge marks.
director.restraintNote: Maintain analytical distance; do not dramatize the supernatural elements as 'magic' but as physical threats. The emotional weight comes from Toren's internal processing, not narration.

cues.delivery: Measured observation of the road's failure; treat 'opinion' as a dry, ironic descriptor.
cues.from: On the eleventh day out of the Level the road stopped being a road and started being an opinion about where a road had once been.
cues.through: It had been a good one. That was the galling part. For six days past Ferrow they had walked on old six-lane with the crown still shedding water and the drainage still, against every reasonable expectation, draining, and Dessa had said on the second morning that if she had known roads like this existed she would have been considerably ruder about the one out of Sallow Creek. Then at about the fourth hour on the eleventh day the surface went soft under Pitch's off hind foot, and the mule stopped, and would not go on, and Dessa took his head and did not argue with him.
cues.reason: Establishes the uncanny nature of the Sag without alarm.

cues.delivery: Rook's commands are flat and immediate; no rising inflection on questions.
cues.from: "Off it," said Rook, from the cart bed.
cues.through: "Off it. All the way off. Take the grass and go wide and don't come back on till I tell you."
cues.reason: Reflects Rook's stoic authority under pressure.

cues.delivery: Rook explains the 'Sag' with weary certainty; pause on 'forty miles across'.
cues.from: Rook had them halt on the shoulder and got himself up onto his elbow and looked back at it for a long time.
cues.through: "South," said Rook. "Out from Meridian. Which is the direction we're going in and I'm not going to pretend otherwise."
cues.reason: Conveys the scale of the threat through Rook's exhaustion.

cues.delivery: Clinical description of ash; Toren's realization that 'nothing killed this' should feel cold.
cues.from: The first was the ash.
cues.through: "No," Rook agreed. "It doesn't."
cues.reason: The horror is in the absence of death, not violence.

cues.delivery: Toren's observation of double shadows; keep the rhythm steady to emphasize the wrongness.
cues.from: They were on the grass with the sun high and the country flat and pale in all directions, and Toren looked down and saw that he had two shadows.
cues.through: It went on for about a minute. Then it thinned, and went, and there was one shadow again, and the light was the light, and nobody said anything for a quarter of a mile.
cues.reason: Avoid 'wonder' tones; treat as a physical anomaly.

cues.delivery: Rook admits ignorance; 'I don't know' must land with heavy finality.
cues.from: "What was that," said Toren.
cues.through: "I have been up and down this country for eleven years," said Rook, "and I have been at a fracture, and I lived in one for four years, and I have never once seen that, and I'm telling you I don't know because the alternative is that I make something up and one of you believes it." He put his forearm over his eyes. "There's a third one coming. There's always a third one."
cues.reason: Subverts the expectation of Rook as an omniscient leader.

cues.delivery: Description of warming iron; Toren's check on the disk should feel like a desperate ritual.
cues.from: The third one was the iron.
cues.through: He took it out about nine times the first night to check. On the tenth time he made himself stop, and put his hand flat on his chest instead, over his shirt, where the disk lay, and the disk was exactly as cold as it had always been, and that was the only thing in four square miles that was behaving itself.
cues.reason: Contrast between the anomalous warmth and the cold disk.

cues.delivery: Narrative shift to training; Rook's physical limitation is a fact of the scene.
cues.from: Rook started him on the struts on the far side of Ferrow and went on with it every day after, from the cart bed, lying down, because he could not stand up for long enough to show anybody anything.
cues.through: It was the worst teaching Toren had ever had from him and the best he had ever seen anybody do. Rook could not demonstrate. He could not walk out ten paces and be in a different place before the sound arrived. All he had was his voice and his eyes and a boy on a verge, and he used all three of them until Toren's legs shook.
cues.reason: Grounds the magical instruction in physical reality.

cues.delivery: Rook's commands are clipped; Toren's internal monologue is rhythmic and frustrated.
cues.from: "Again."
cues.through: He let the struts go and reached for the spike and it came.
cues.reason: Reflects the repetitive nature of training.

cues.delivery: Rook's explanation of 'changeover' is technical; pause on the number 'one'.
cues.from: "Count it," said Rook.
cues.through: "That's exactly what it should be for a boy who's been Ember since the spring, and if it were much better I'd be worried about what you'd been doing in the night." He shifted, carefully, and did not quite hide what it cost him. "Do it again tomorrow and the day after. It'll come down to one. It won't come down past one."
cues.reason: Emphasizes the limitation of Toren's ability.

cues.delivery: Rook corrects Toren; 'No' is a hard stop to the boy's ambition.
cues.from: "Then I'll make it come down past one."
cues.through: "I know what it isn't. Put the spike away and get the struts up and do it eleven more times, and then come and hold my arm while I get down off this cart, because I'd rather that was you than Wyck."
cues.reason: Reinforces Rook's role as the teacher of harsh truths.

cues.delivery: Dialogue about the culvert; silence is heavy with unspoken grief.
cues.from: It was nobody's fault and it was a small thing. The six-lane went into a cut with the walls close, and there was a culvert under it, an arched brick mouth eight feet high with black water going through it a foot deep, and Rook wanted to know if it was walkable because the alternative was a half-mile of the soft ground on the crown. Dessa had the best eyes. Dessa went down the bank on the stick and stood at the mouth of it and looked into a hole that went about nine feet and then stopped being anything.
cues.through: "With what," said Dessa. "There's no wood in four miles. We've been burning dung for two days."
cues.reason: The pause before Milo's name carries the emotional weight.

cues.delivery: Toren starts to speak; stop abruptly. The silence is shared grief.
cues.from: There was a short silence on that bank, and it went on about two seconds too long, and then everybody understood at the same time why it had gone on two seconds too long, and Toren heard himself say, into it, in a perfectly ordinary voice, "Milo would—"
cues.through: Nobody helped him. That was the thing he thought about afterward, lying awake: that not one of the four of them said a single word to get him off it, and it was not cruelty, it was that all four of them had been about to say the same thing and had got to it a half-second later than he had, and there was nothing on that bank to say.
cues.reason: The interruption marks the collective trauma.

cues.delivery: Dessa's declaration is matter-of-fact; no heroism in her voice.
cues.from: Dessa came back up. "It's walkable," she said. "It's walkable because I'm going to say it's walkable, and I'll go first, and if I'm wrong I'll be wet."
cues.through: They walked it. It was walkable. It took nine minutes and it was the longest nine minutes of the day, and Toren went through it with his hand out flat against wet brick on the right-hand side and the spike out in his left where it gave off exactly no light at all, and had never given off any light at all, and never would, because it was an Edge and an Edge is a thing you put into something, and the boy who had carried the light through Coldwater and the orchard and the reed beds and out along a sluice wall in the dark on his own judgement had been dead for sixteen days.
cues.reason: Reflects Dessa's pragmatic nature.

cues.delivery: Toren crying; narration is observational and detached from the emotion.
cues.from: He went out past the cart after they made camp and got about forty paces and sat down on the rail.
cues.through: It went on a long time. It was not dignified and there was nothing in it he recognised. He had been sick behind a wall on the bank at the Level and that had been a thing his body did to him; this was a thing he was doing, and he could not stop it, and about four minutes in he stopped wanting to.
cues.reason: Maintains narrator distance while describing raw grief.

cues.delivery: Wyck's conversation is flat; he shares his burden without seeking sympathy.
cues.from: He heard Wyck come up the road and stop about six feet away.
cues.through: "I don't know. Ask me in a year."
cues.reason: Reflects Wyck's stoic character.

cues.delivery: Wyck's monologue about Milo; dry humor mixed with pain.
cues.from: "He was annoying," said Wyck.
cues.through: "It was not very good, it was extremely unfair, he did the voice like I'm a hundred and four—" Wyck stopped again, and made a sound that was not a laugh and was not the other thing either, and sat there with the bar across his knees. "Right," he said.
cues.reason: Captures the complexity of their shared grief.

cues.delivery: Toren's realization at Hallam Cross; 'cold from the back of his neck down'.
cues.from: In the morning they came to the flyover at Hallam Cross.
cues.through: These were at the height of his head. They were longer than his arm. They had gone through the rail and out the other side of it and four inches into the concrete of the pier behind, and the concrete was old and the cuts in it were bright.
cues.reason: Physical reaction to a known threat.

cues.delivery: Rook's command to Dessa; urgent but controlled.
cues.from: "That's the same thing," said Toren. "That's the—"
cues.through: Dessa went up the rail on the stick, counting.
cues.reason: Reflects the tactical urgency of the moment.

cues.delivery: Dessa's counting; Rook's final command is a whisper of dread.
cues.from: Dessa got to eight feet and there was nothing.
cues.through: "Get everything off the crown of the road," he said, "and get it in behind the revetments, and do it now, and do it quietly, and Toren — put that spike away and leave it away. It comes at worked power. Everything does. That one'll come at it from four miles."
cues.reason: The silence after the count emphasizes the threat.

pauses.reason: Emphasize the uncanny nature of the road's failure.

For six days past Ferrow they had walked on old six-lane with the crown still shedding water and the drainage still, against every reasonable expectation, draining, and Dessa had said on the second morning that if she had known roads like this existed she would have been considerably ruder about the one out of Sallow Creek. pauses.reason: Completed thought on road failure; allow listener to process the uncanny nature of the Sag.

pauses.after: "Off it. All the way off. Take the grass and go wide and don't come back on till I tell you."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset after Rook's command; transition back to narrative action.

pauses.after: "That's a name I heard in a flax shed six days ago from a man who's ninety, and he heard it from a carter, and the carter said it was eleven miles across and moving." He lay back down. "So it's forty miles across and it's been moving for two years and there's nobody to ask. That's the whole of what I've got and I'd rather you had it than not."
pauses.reason: Completed thought on the scale of the Sag; pause for impact.
Highlight the scale of the threat described by Rook.

pauses.after: There was nothing in it. It was clean the way flour is clean, the whole length of the ditch, and once Toren had seen that he could not stop seeing it, and he opened his hands and let it go and climbed back up out of the ditch and wiped his palms on his coat twice.
pauses.reason: Major realization that 'nothing killed this'; allow dread to land.
Prepare listener for the reversal in understanding ash origin.
Emphasize the physical anomaly Toren observes.

pauses.after: Everything had two. The cart had two. Pitch had two, and one of them had four legs and the other one had four legs, and that was somehow much worse than if it hadn't.
pauses.reason: Completed thought on the double shadows; pause for tension.

pauses.after: "I have been up and down this country for eleven years," said Rook, "and I have been at a fracture, and I lived in one for four years, and I have never once seen that, and I'm telling you I don't know because the alternative is that I make something up and one of you believes it." He put his forearm over his eyes. "There's a third one coming. There's always a third one."
pauses.reason: Rook's admission of ignorance; significant character beat requiring silence.

pauses.reason: Completed thought on the disk and iron warmth; transition to training scene.

pauses.after: Toren counted it. He did it eleven times, standing on a verge in the wrong-lit afternoon with the iron of the cart warm behind him, and the best he ever got was one and a half, and the honest number was closer to two.
pauses.reason: Toren's internal realization of his limitation; pause for reflection.
Emphasize the specific limitation in Toren's training progress.

pauses.after: "With what," said Dessa. "There's no wood in four miles. We've been burning dung for two days."
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing on the silence regarding Milo; deep breath required.
Prepare for the emotional weight of Milo's name and its interruption.

pauses.after: They sat on the rail. Out in the field on the left something small went through the grass and stopped.
pauses.reason: Speaker reset after Wyck's monologue; transition to Toren's reaction.

pauses.after: There were four lines gouged down through the rail.
pauses.reason: Completed thought on the gouge marks; pause for recognition of threat.
Emphasize the visual detail that triggers Toren's recognition of threat.

pauses.after: "Ninety-one," she said. "And then eleven feet past that there's another one, and then nothing again for a long way, and I didn't go and look."
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing on Dessa's count and Rook's silence; heavy dread.
Highlight the specific count and its ominous implication for the creature's movement.
